mission: Make every external learning source useful as a benchmark lens while building Buddy's original, evidence-backed capability graph and a software-engineering mastery track.

source_policy.rule: All 1000 sources must earn their place by contributing measurable capability, benchmark, professional-task, or validation value. A source is not valuable merely because it is popular.

software_engineer_mastery.goal: Build evidence of software-engineering competence as closely as practical without claiming an accredited degree, professional license, employer credential, or certification that Buddy or a user has not actually earned.
software_engineer_mastery.credential_boundary: Use mastery scores and portfolio evidence to estimate readiness. Never label the result as a government, university, employer, or professional certification.

three_core_lenses.role: real repository workflow and software delivery evidence
occupation tasks, skills, work activities, abilities, knowledge and professional-role mapping
structured programming curriculum, projects, quizzes and career-oriented skill progression

beneficial_benchmark_example.challenge: Take a vague business request and turn it into a secure, tested, documented application.
beneficial_benchmark_example.score: 0-100 evidence-backed score by domain plus confidence and limitations

anti_shortcut: Passing source-specific exercises is insufficient. Buddy must transfer knowledge into original tasks that were not copied from the learning source.
north_star: Use the best 1000 sources as teachers and benchmark lenses, then make Buddy prove its skills through original work, professional task simulations, reproducible tests, and increasingly difficult engineering systems.
